themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints spiked to 137 THIS WEEK, a 260% increase from the 38.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.33), suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or seasonal weather damage requiring urgent investigation of which streets are failing and why.
evidence: 137 Street Condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 38.0 weekly average (260% spike, z-score 7.33)
Spike is statistically significant at highest severity level
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'Inspect sanitary sewer on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed,' indicating known structural issues
reporting_angles: Identify which streets are generating the bulk of complaints this week and conduct visual inspection
Interview DOT about whether recent weather, construction, or deferred maintenance triggered the spike
Examine whether this spike aligns with seasonal thaw damage or a localized sewer/subsurface failure

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Violations Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Food Establishment complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, a 367% spike from the 1.5 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.5), indicating potential new health code violations or inspection activity at local restaurants and food vendors.
evidence: 7 Food Establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (367% spike, z-score 5.5)
First appearance of Food Establishment in top spikes list suggests new pattern
Spike is sudden and concentrated in current week, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Obtain DOHMH inspection records for Ridgewood/Glendale area this week to identify specific establishments and violations
Interview Department of Health about whether there was a targeted inspection blitz or complaints about a specific incident
Determine if spike is tied to a particular food vendor, restaurant chain, or neighborhood food market

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints hit 58 LAST WEEK, a 572% spike from the 8.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 11.48), indicating sustained disruptive activity (construction, vendors, vehicles, or street events) that residents are actively reporting.
evidence: 58 Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.6 weekly average (572% spike, z-score 11.48)
Statistically one of the most extreme spikes in dataset (z-score 11.48)
Paired with 83% spike in Noise - Residential complaints (111 vs. 60.6 avg), suggesting district-wide noise problem
reporting_angles: Canvass Ridgewood/Glendale streets to identify source(s) of noise: active construction projects, street vendors, event spaces, or traffic pattern changes
Interview NYPD about noise complaints and enforcement activity last week
Check DOB permits for active construction sites that may be operating outside permitted hours

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Complaints Up 83%
themes_detail.summary: Residential Noise complaints increased to 111 LAST WEEK, up 83% from the 60.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.37), suggesting indoor/apartment noise disturbances from neighbors, music, or mechanical systems affecting habitability.
evidence: 111 Noise - Residential complaints LAST WEEK vs. 60.6 weekly average (83% spike, z-score 6.37)
Convergence: both residential and street/sidewalk noise spiking simultaneously suggests district-wide noise event or change
High z-score (6.37) indicates this is a statistically significant departure from baseline
reporting_angles: Interview residents in multi-family buildings about whether noise complaints relate to specific neighbors, parties, or nightlife venues
Cross-reference with Noise - Commercial spike (408 total complaints) to identify if bar/club hours or new venue opened
Determine if spike correlates with warmer weather, new tenant move-ins, or change in enforcement

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Complaints: Dumpsters & Litter
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster and litter basket complaints spiked 3 weeks ago (7 and 3 complaints respectively, +833% and +700% from baselines), with Dumpster spike sustained, suggesting ongoing waste management or illegal dumping problems in the district.
evidence: Dumpster Complaint: 7 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly average (+833% spike, z-score 9.45)
Litter Basket Request: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (+700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Both spikes are older than street condition and food establishment spikes, but remain in high-severity range
reporting_angles: Determine if spikes were tied to a specific location (park, commercial corridor, residential block) or district-wide
Interview DSNY about whether there was a missed collection, contractor issue, or illegal dumping incident 3 weeks ago
Check whether spike has subsided or if it represents a new baseline for ongoing sanitation problems
